_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); semiconductor signals with NVIDIA's rule-T thresholds; the listing rule (NVDA listed 1999-01-22)

pit_profile.why: 'NVIDIA is dedicated to advancing visual computing.' 'The market for our products is intensely competitive and is characterized by rapid technological change, evolving industry standards and declining average selling prices.' Its current competitors include 'suppliers of discrete and integrated GPUs, including supercomputers and chipsets that incorporate 3D graphics functionality as part of their existing solutions, such as Advanced Micro Devices, or AMD, and Intel Corporation, or Intel' (FY2015 10-K); CYCLICAL kept: this 10-K no longer calls the business cyclical (the FY2014 10-K's risk factor 'Our business is cyclical in nature' is gone), and the kind stands (the BKR FY2015 rule; the class label only); no theme in taxonomy_eras.json covers GPUs integrated into other processors, so those words stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

classification.quality_note: 'NVIDIA is dedicated to advancing visual computing.' 'The market for our products is intensely competitive and is characterized by rapid technological change, evolving industry standards and declining average selling prices.' Its current competitors include 'suppliers of discrete and integrated GPUs, including supercomputers and chipsets that incorporate 3D graphics functionality as part of their existing solutions, such as Advanced Micro Devices, or AMD, and Intel Corporation, or Intel' (FY2015 10-K); CYCLICAL kept: this 10-K no longer calls the business cyclical (the FY2014 10-K's risk factor 'Our business is cyclical in nature' is gone), and the kind stands (the BKR FY2015 rule; the class label only); no theme in taxonomy_eras.json covers GPUs integrated into other processors, so those words stay here (the PEP obesity rule). cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 0.84x; +27% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +0.01; conservative 2yr +11%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -17.8%/yr (worst year FY06-FY15 ex-FY09 ex-FY10, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS -8.7%/yr (Q2 FY16 guide YoY + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr ex-FY09 ex-FY10 median

BULL.desc: EPS +8.2%/yr (FY06-FY15 ex-FY09 ex-FY10 CAGR, at least BASE); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +54.3%/yr (best 2-yr run FY06-FY15 ex-FY09 ex-FY10, at least BULL); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: NVDA (retrospective, 2015-07-31) ◎ ACCUMULATE — Ratio B 0.84x (44.0% downside to Bear $11.17 / +52.3% upside to Bull $30.39) | Adj composite 2.37 vs market 2.36: gap +0.01 [FAIRLY VALUED] | +27% above the EPP floor $15.68 (14x FY16E $1.12) | Conservative 2-yr case: +10.7% total (+5.3%/yr) | At 17.8x FY16E the 15% hurdle price $26.38 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; revenue +4.4% YoY in Q1 FY16, forward revenues -10.2% to -6.6% (Q2 FY16 revenue guide (Q1 FY16 release)); no disruption theme has dated evidence.
